headlines.article_text: YouTube sports strategy targets more live rights -- but not necessarily events Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points YouTube is scanning the live sports landscape with interest in buying more rights. One strategy of YouTube's is to air some games on its massive free service and put most games on its subscription Premium service. YouTube is still wrestling with the feasibility of becoming the hub of all local games for the NBA starting in 2027. Subscribe here to get access today . Photo illustration of the YouTube TV logo displayed on a smartphone, with the YouTube logo in the background. Nurphoto | Nurphoto | Getty Images YouTube is stalking the sports landscape for live rights. YouTube would like as many games as it can get its hands on – while also giving users as "clean" of an experience as possible, according to people familiar with the matter. YouTube has been coy with its sports strategy, acquiring the rights to one NFL game last year for its free, ad-supported platform and buying "NFL Sunday Ticket" rights until the end of the 2029-30 season. Beyond those two moves, YouTube has largely been quiet. Still, YouTube is an interested buyer in live sports for almost all of the major U.S. sports leagues if it can get bespoke rights that present an easy consumer message, such as all local games or all games in a tournament, said the people, who asked not to be named because the company's plans are private. YouTube's strategy is distinct from Netflix's — an interesting contrast between the two largest streaming services in the world by users. While Netflix wants individual games or tournaments that it can turn into mini-events, YouTube is more likely to buy games in bulk if there's a clear consumer proposition underlying the rights. In other words, YouTube isn't interested in a swath of games if there's no obvious connection to them. Sports Business Journal reported earlier this year that YouTube is in advanced talks to be the NBA's new regional sports network solution, buying the rights for 20 to 25 teams for a price tag of potentially more than $1 billion. YouTube is interested in the FIFA Men's World Cup rights, as CNBC first reported in July. YouTube is still wrestling with the feasibility of this idea if it can't get all of the teams, said the people. YouTube ideally wants both in-market and out-of-market games, the people said. It's also unclear if the NBA is comfortable selling complete rights to one platform. A big part of YouTube's sports objective relates to building up its premium service. A few weeks ago, YouTube Premium struck a deal to ingest Peacock content within the service for no extra cost. YouTube Premium, which eliminates YouTube ads and costs $15.99 per month, doesn't necessarily want to strike a bunch of other similar deals and turn the service into an aggregator of other companies' streaming services. But what may interest YouTube executives is buying a chunk of live sports and putting it behind the paywall. In other words, making people pay for YouTube Premium to get access to the games. YouTube could then use "free" YouTube as its front-of-the-paywall marketing tool to get people to pay the monthly subscription fee for YouTube Premium. For example, it could put a small number of games on ad-supported YouTube to effectively advertise for signing up for the full package in Premium. It also can use its millions of sports-related content creator videos to push live games on Premium. YouTube hired Justin Connolly away from Disney last year to be its global head of media and sports. Connolly was one of Disney's highest paid executives, having spent 25 years at the company and rising through the ranks to become the company's president of platform distribution, including ESPN and Disney+. headlines.article_text: Accenture stock rallies after earnings beat expectations Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Earnings and revenue for fiscal Q4 beat expectations. The company posted a record in big-ticket client bookings, while also increasing its quarterly dividend. In this article ACN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT VIDEO 10:14 10:14 Watch CNBC's full interview with Accenture CEO Julie Sweet Shares of Accenture surged Thursday after the company's fiscal fourth-quarter results beat estimates. The consulting giant reported earnings per share of $3.29 on revenue of $18.68 billion. That exceeded LSEG consensus estimates of $3.18 earnings per share and revenue of $18.03 billion. The stock surged more than 22% at one point, but ended the day up close to 16%. In an exclusive interview on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street," Accenture CEO Julie Sweet said AI has served as a key growth driver for the business as it accumulates partners in key AI sectors such as data centers and capital infrastructure. "We've just finished the year with $85 billion of new business going into next year, and that is driven by our growth strategy to focus on big transformational deals and making sure we're the winner in AI and data," Sweet told CNBC. "We're investing now to not only be the partner for companies who are going to scale across the enterprise, but also to be relevant to all parts of things that have to enable the use of AI." Full year adjusted earnings for fiscal 2026 amounted to $13.97 per share, up 8% year on year, while revenue totaled $74.2 billion, marking a 6% increase. ACN 5-day chart "These results reflect the continued trust our clients place in us to help them reinvent and create value, the high level of innovation we bring every day and the extraordinary commitment of our Reinventors to our clients' success," Sweet said in a press release Thursday, noting broad-based growth across the business and record cash returned to shareholders. The company also posted a record in big-ticket client bookings, those valuing $100 million or more. On top of that, Accenture increased its quarterly dividend by 5% to $1.71 per share, which will be payable Nov. 13. For its fiscal-year 2027 outlook, Accenture sees 3%-6% year-over-year growth in both revenue and adjusted earnings per share. Following the beat, Stifel reiterated its buy rating of the professional services company and increased the stock's price target to $242 per share, up from $225. Analyst David Grossman pointed to broad-based outperformance in the stock due to smaller discretionary deals as well as activity in the federal government sector and accelerating demand from AI-related partners, showcasing stability in the company's business model. "In our view, ACN is the only professional services provider at scale that has demonstrated an ability to consistently re-skill around different technology and business cycles," Grossman wrote in the note. Despite Thursday's massive gain, the stock remains down more than 18% year to date due to worries that artificial intelligence will disrupt key business segments.
